paper-figure's SKILL has the main session check its tables against the result
JSON and then touch figures/TABLE_DATA_CHECK_PASSED.txt, but the engine only
trusted a receipt written after its *own* paid verification session, so every
figure step paid for a second check. A marker this session created or touched
(absent or different before the main call) is bound to the current snapshot
here, before any repair. A stale marker from an earlier run is not; any later
table/JSON change invalidates the fingerprint and the paid check runs as before;
record_review itself refuses on a deterministic fatal.

Run the deterministic PDF visual gate for the requested figure subset.
The model saying that a chart "looks fine" is not evidence.  This guard
inspects the files that actually landed in ``figures/`` and runs locally,
so it adds no model calls or token cost.  ``candidates`` may contain source
names, PNG paths or PDF paths; only corresponding existing PDFs are passed
to the checker.  A PNG-only Word workflow is therefore left compatible.
Which Skill's paper submission contract gates this step.
The improvement loop rewrites the whole competition paper.  In PDF mode it
runs after the last compiler and recompiles ``paper/main.pdf``; nothing
downstream checks it again, so it must pass that compiler's full contract
(rendered pages included).  In DOCX mode it edits ``paper/main.md`` and
passes the DOCX writer's source contract (export checks once more).
Every other step gates on its own Skill name; names outside
CONTRACT_SKILLS stay not-applicable, exactly as before.

Classify a failed runner result and return ``(kind, retry_budget)``.
The budget is the number of *additional* model processes allowed.  It does
not weaken any output gate: after the budget is exhausted the step fails
visibly instead of repeatedly submitting an identical request.
Return a content signature for declared artifacts only.
Diagnostic reports and logs are deliberately excluded: rewriting a check
report is not progress toward a missing paper, result file, or figure.
Timestamps are deliberately excluded too: an agent that rewrites identical
content has made no repair progress and must not earn another paid retry.

Per-problem result files that themselves say the solve did not succeed.
Only the file's own top-level declaration counts — status failed/error, a
traceback or exception text, an error *message* string — or a file with no
results at all.  Values inside the results are never interpreted: a numeric
``error`` metric, ``infeasible`` or a time-limit status can be legitimate.

``paper/main.tex`` is often only an assembly file whose real content lives
under ``paper/sections``.  Measuring the root alone falsely classified a
complete split manuscript as an empty shell and launched paid retries.
